rejected_prebaseline_instrument.reason: Direct Python wait4 inherited the Python parent memory high-water mark, obscuring workload memory. Replaced with a native supervisor and a required allocation calibration before full measurements.

boundaries: Measurements are GNU release on the recorded shared WSL2 machine; other profiles/targets received correctness smoke checks, not performance acceptance.
No absolute latency/memory budgets, doubling/scaling acceptance, 10-percent regression gate, or 1000-run stress claim is established.
Peak RSS is Linux whole-process high-water resident memory, not exclusive allocation accounting. Timings and memory have the boundaries in docs/performance.md.
Inputs use warm filesystem caches. Source I/O includes parsing and fresh run setup; waiting includes a 10 ms hold after all runs enter.
Historical worker-startup and musl timing observations in docs/async-execution-evidence.json and docs/nonblocking-io-evidence.json remain open. None recurred in these four full test suites.
Hosted CI has not been observed; its added smoke/helper steps were executed locally.
